title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is analysing level-4 structures on elliptic curves. M is a free Z/4Z-module of rank 2 (think E[4]), M_0 = M/2M, and J = M_0^* minus 0, the 3 nonzero forms. On earlier pages he attached to M an octahedron Δ_M. Its 6 vertices are the 6 cyclic subgroups of order 4, i.e. P^1(Z/4). Opposite vertices have the same image in M_0, which gives the 3 axes Δ_i, i ∈ J. Its 8 faces F(Δ) = ∏_i Δ_i form a torsor under F_2^J. Antipody σ_Δ = ε_Δ is the diagonal element. He proved Aut_oct(Δ_M) ≅ GL(M)/{±1}, the full octahedral group O_h ≅ S_4 × C_2 of order 48 = 96/2, and noted that its abelianisation is F_2 × F_2.

This page names the three nontrivial F_2-torsors (two-element sets) cut out by the three nontrivial characters of O_h:
(i) Or(Δ), the two orientations of the octahedron. Its character is det (nontrivial on antipody, trivial on rotations).
(ii) ω_Δ = ω_{I_Δ}, the two orientations (sign-classes of orderings) of the set I_Δ = F(Δ)/σ_Δ of 4 face directions (equivalently the 4 body diagonals of the dual cube). Its character is the sign of the permutation action, the nontrivial character of Aut^+ ≅ S_4.
(iii) C_Δ, the two checkerboard colourings of the faces, equivalently the two tetrahedra inscribed in the dual cube. Its character is the product sg·det, with kernel T_d.
NB: F(Δ) ≅ C_Δ × I_Δ. (41): since the three characters multiply to 1, Or ∧ ω ∧ C ≅ the trivial torsor.
(42) describes C_Δ as the contracted product ∧_i Δ_i, i.e. F(Δ) pushed out along the sum map F_2^J → F_2, whose kernel is ≅ M_0. So C_Δ = F(Δ)/M_0 = P_M/(M_0 × Z).
(43) identifies ω_Δ with ω_J, the orientation torsor of the 3-element set J, via the canonical S_4 → S_3 = GL(M_0). Under GL(M) this is the character sg(g) obtained through GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3.
(44) gives Or(Δ) ≅ ω ∧ C ≅ μ := [det M]^*, the set of generators of the rank-one Z/4-module Λ^2 M. This corresponds to the character det: GL(M) → (Z/4)^* = {±1}. Hence also C_Δ ≅ μ ∧ ω.
Finally he begins defining the canonical oriented octahedron Δ^+ attached to M, as the quotient of P_M by antipody, which is a torsor under M_0. This is continued on the next page (45)-(48) toward lifting GL_2(Z/4)' = GL_2(Z/4)/{±1}-torsors to GL_2(Z/4)-torsors.

Arithmetic meaning, implicit: for an elliptic curve, μ ↔ μ_4 via the Weil pairing (the field Q(i)), ω_J ↔ √disc (the sign of Galois on E[2]), and C ↔ their product (√(−disc)).
errors: No mathematical error is apparent. The character assignments check out: det(−1) = −1 and sg(−1) = 1; a mirror reflection in T_d has det = −1 and acts as a transposition on the diagonals, so sg·det is trivial on T_d, consistent with C ↔ sg·det.
The phrase 'correspond des cos. ... de Aut^+_oct(Δ)×{1,σ_Δ}' is loose. The colouring character is the product character, nontrivial on both factors, not a coset of one factor.

ideas.what: Octahedral model of GL_2(Z/4)/±1 ≅ O_h ≅ S_4×C_2 acting on P^1(Z/4) (6 vertices, 3 axes indexed by 2-torsion)
ideas.modern_name: octahedral symmetry of level-4 structure / X(4) (Klein)
ideas.usually_credited_to: F. Klein (octahedral group and the level-4 modular curve), classical

ideas.what: Three quadratic torsors from the abelianisation (Z/2)^2 of the octahedral group (orientation, sign on 4 diagonals, checkerboard colouring) with trivial triple contracted product
ideas.modern_name: quadratic characters of GL_2(Z/4); torsor contracted products

ideas.what: Orientation torsor of the octahedron ≅ generators of det M (Weil pairing μ_4); face-direction sign ≅ sign torsor of the 2-torsion (√disc)
ideas.modern_name: det and sign characters of GL_2(Z/4); Q(i) and Q(√Δ) inside Q(E[4])

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, canonical torsor-theoretic bookkeeping of the octahedral picture of level-4 structures. It is elegant and personal in style, but its mathematical content (O_h ≅ GL_2(Z/4)/±1, its three quadratic characters, det ↔ Weil pairing) is classical.
transcription_corrections: 'cocaractère non trivial de Aut^+_oct(Δ)' should read 'caractère non trivial de Aut^+_oct(Δ)'.
The antipody is written σ_Δ here, the same element as ε_Δ / a_Δ on the neighbouring pages.
In (42) the quotient reads P_M/(M_0×Z), with Z = {±id} the centre.
